knowledgeAnswers.rationale: WorkSafe Victoria states that respiratory protection is needed where higher controls do not keep exposures at or below the standards. It is the last layer.
WorkSafe Victoria states that a half-face, non-disposable respirator with a P2 filter is usually sufficient for wood dust.
A facial-seal respirator needs a fit check each time it is put on to confirm a good seal against the face.
A bearded worker cannot be fit checked on a facial-seal respirator, so the assessment selects another option, such as a PAPR, or the task waits.
NSW LeadSmart warns that simple paper masks may not protect against fine dust, and advises an AS-1716-approved respirator or P1 or P2 filters.

practicalCriteria: Candidate selects a respirator and filter from the assessment and checks its markings against AS/NZS 1716 or an equivalent.
Candidate completes a fit check on a facial-seal respirator before use, and records it.
Candidate identifies a user with facial hair that breaks the seal, and stops the task until another option is selected.
Candidate cleans and stores the respirator outside the work area and records the issue and training.
passRule: Knowledge checks: at least 80% correct (4 of 5). Practical sign-off is separate. A knowledge pass does not establish practical competence, and the practical criteria must be observed and recorded by an assessor. Fit testing is assessed only where the program allows it.
evidenceRequired: Respirator issue and fit test record
Training record for the respirator program
Assessor observation of the fit check
stopWorkCriteria: Facial-seal respirator used without a fit check
Facial-seal respirator used on a user with facial hair that breaks the seal
Paper mask used in place of the assessed respirator
